Here's the file as requested.

```markdown
---
name: company-handbook
description: Use for anything related to our company.
---

# Company Handbook

Single reference for engineering, operations, HR policy, marketing, and internal terminology. Find the relevant section below and follow it.

## Contents
1. Code Style (Python, TypeScript)
2. Deploy Process and Rollback
3. On-Call Runbook
4. PTO and Expense Policy
5. Brand Voice Guide
6. Org Chart and Contacts
7. Glossary

## 1. Code Style (~600 lines)
### 1.1 Python
### 1.2 TypeScript
### 1.3 Shared conventions (naming, tests, reviews)

## 2. Deploy Process and Rollback (~400 lines)
### 2.1 General deploy checklist
### 2.2 Service A
### 2.3 Service B
### 2.4 Service C
### 2.5 Service D
### 2.6 Rollback steps (per service)

## 3. On-Call Runbook (~900 lines)
### 3.1 Escalation and paging basics
### 3.2 Alert: <alert-1> ... through <alert-35>
(each: symptoms, likely cause, first actions, escalation)

## 4. PTO and Expense Policy (~300 lines)
### 4.1 PTO accrual and requests
### 4.2 Expense categories and limits
### 4.3 Reimbursement process

## 5. Brand Voice Guide (~250 lines)
### 5.1 Tone principles
### 5.2 Do / don't examples
### 5.3 Channel-specific guidance

## 6. Org Chart and Contacts (~200 lines)
### 6.1 Leadership
### 6.2 Teams and owners
### 6.3 Contact directory

## 7. Glossary (~350 lines)
### 7.1 Terms A–Z
```

Paste each section's content under its heading and you're done.

Before you ship, three things may be worth a quick conversation with the eng lead. None of them require a redesign:

1. **Context cost.** The whole body loads whenever the skill triggers. With that description, it will trigger on almost everything, so a 3,000-line file lands in context even for a one-line code style question. That dilutes attention and can make answers worse, not better.
2. **Phone numbers.** Personal phone numbers in a file that's loaded into model context and probably committed to a repo is a privacy exposure. Consider linking to your HR directory instead.
3. **Brand voice and PTO** are likely irrelevant to engineering work, so they'd be pure noise in those sessions.

If you want a cheap middle path that's still one day of work: keep this single file as a short index (~30 lines) and move each section into its own file next to it (`code-style.md`, `runbook.md`, and so on). Then the description can say what's in them, and Claude reads only what it needs. You'd still maintain one skill, and the content is the same. I can draft that version if you'd like.
